circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: The Yas Marina Circuit is a 5. 281 km track on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi, designed by Hermann Tilke, and has served as the venue for the season-closing Abu Dhabi Grand Prix since 2009. It represents the second Formula One facility established in the Middle East, following Bahrain's circuit and preceding later additions in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: A street circuit encircling Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb, this track hosts the Formula One Australian Grand Prix each year alongside supporting motorsport categories. The venue holds an FIA Grade 1 licence and serves as a premier destination for international racing competition.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit was originally established as the Österreichring and served as the venue for the Austrian Grand Prix throughout the 1970s and 1980s. Following a redesign and shortening, the track was renamed and eventually returned to hosting the Austrian Grand Prix from 1997 onwards.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street track in Azerbaijan's capital, spanning 6. 003 km and ranking as the fourth-longest venue in Formula One. The circuit hosted its first F1 race in 2016 as the European Grand Prix, before becoming the permanent home of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 2017 onwards.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit spans 5. 412 km and hosted the inaugural Formula One grand prix held in the Middle East that same year. The venue, holding an FIA Grade 1 license, accommodates various motorsport categories including GP2 racing and endurance competitions, while featuring multiple circuit configurations.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, this 4. 657-kilometre circuit combines extended straight sections with diverse corner configurations, making it a versatile test for all racing disciplines. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification and can accommodate approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstand facilities.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: The 7. 004 km Belgian circuit hosting the Formula One Belgian Grand Prix has continuously staged races since 1985, with only two exceptions in 2003 and 2006. Located near the town of Spa in the Wallonia region, this track has deep historical roots in motorsport, having first welcomed a Grand Prix competition in 1925 and participated in the inaugural F1 world championship season in 1950.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, Quebec, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve is a 4. 361 km track that hosts the FIA Formula One Canadian Grand Prix. Beyond Formula One, the circuit has accommodated various international racing series including sportscar championships and North American open-wheel and stock car competitions.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading District, this Chinese motorsport venue hosted the country's premier Formula One race annually between 2004 and 2019 before resuming in 2024. The track has also begun accommodating electric racing events from 2024 onwards, diversifying its international motorsport calendar.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Located near villages in Northamptonshire, Silverstone has been England's premier racing venue since inaugurating the British Grand Prix in 1948 and hosting the inaugural World Championship race two years later. After alternating with two other circuits between 1955 and 1986, the British Grand Prix became a permanent fixture at Silverstone from 1987 onwards.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring near Budapest became the first Formula One circuit to host a Grand Prix behind the Iron Curtain when it inaugurated in 1986, constructed remarkably quickly in just eight months outside the Hungarian capital. This 4. 381 km permanent track was built after plans for a Monaco-style street circuit in Budapest's largest park were rejected by the government in favor of a purpose-built venue near a major highway.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: The Autodromo Nazionale Monza is a 5. 793 km Italian racing circuit established in 1922 as Europe's oldest purpose-built motorsport venue, renowned as "the Temple of Speed" for its extensive straights and rapid corners. Home to the Italian Grand Prix since 1949 (except during 1980 renovations), it remains one of only four tracks to feature continuously on the Formula One calendar from the championship's inception.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Located in Mie Prefecture, Japan, Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807 km motorsport venue operated by Honda Mobilityland that hosts major international racing events. The track holds 155,000 spectators and is particularly renowned for hosting Formula One and Japanese Super Formula championship races.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course situated in Paradise, Nevada, that navigates through the heart of Las Vegas's famous boulevard lined with major resort properties. The layout features several iconic venues and landmarks within the circuit, creating a unique urban racing environment that showcases the city's most recognizable hotels and entertainment destinations.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: This 4. 304 km Mexico City circuit honours two Mexican racing brothers, Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez, both of whom died in racing accidents in the 1960s and 1970s. The track has returned to hosting Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix since 2015 on its current layout, having previously staged the race during two earlier periods ending in 1992.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, featuring a 3. 363-mile layout with 19 corners that generates qualifying speeds near 139 mph. Designed by specialist racing architects for the 2022 Miami Grand Prix addition to the Formula One calendar, the venue serves primarily as a Formula One racing facility while also hosting modified configurations for other motorsport competitions.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Monaco Grand Prix takes place on a street circuit measuring 3. 337 km that winds through the Monte Carlo and La Condamine districts, incorporating the harbour area of the principality. Though officially known as the Circuit de Monaco, the track is typically called "Monte Carlo" after the neighbourhood that encompasses most of its layout.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the dunes near the Dutch coast, roughly 35 kilometers west of Amsterdam, Circuit Zandvoort is a 4. 259 km track that hosted the revival of the Dutch Grand Prix starting in 2021 before concluding its Formula One tenure in 2026. The venue, situated north of the seaside town of Zandvoort, has operated under various names throughout its history.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: Located north of Doha in Qatar, Lusail International Circuit is a 5. 419-kilometer track featuring a 1. 068-kilometer main straight and holding FIA Grade 1 status.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos is a 4. 309 km Brazilian motorsport facility in São Paulo that opened in 1940 and was later renamed in 1985 to commemorate the late Formula 1 driver José Carlos Pace. The track operates in a counterclockwise direction and features an onsite kart circuit dedicated to another legendary Brazilian racing driver.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street racing venue positioned along Jeddah's waterfront adjacent to the Red Sea in Saudi Arabia. Since its debut in 2021, it has served as the home of the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix, while also hosting Formula E racing from 2025 onwards.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's downtown and Kallang districts, utilizing public roads around the Marina Bay waterfront for racing.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located near Barcelona in northeastern Spain, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya stretches 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced mix of lengthy straights and diverse corner configurations, making it a comprehensive test of driver skill. The venue holds an FIA Grade 1 license and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its facilities.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: Located in Austin, Texas, the Circuit of the Americas is a 3. 426-mile FIA Grade 1 facility that serves as the permanent home of the Formula One United States Grand Prix. Beyond its marquee F1 event, the track hosts multiple international racing series including MotoGP and the Lone Star Le Mans endurance race, though it has previously accommodated various other motorsport championships ranging from IndyCar to rallycross competitions.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Thai-British driver Alexander Albon represents Thailand in Formula One, currently racing for the Williams team.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: The Spanish driver competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, having secured two world championships during his tenure with Renault in 2005 and 2006, along with 32 race victories over 23 seasons. Beyond single-seater racing, Alonso has achieved significant success in endurance competition, including two Le Mans victories and the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship, making him the sole driver to have won both a Formula One world title and a world sportscar championship.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Andrea Kimi Antonelli, an Italian driver, made his Formula One debut in 2025 with Mercedes, where he currently races. The driver has secured eight Grand Prix victories during his early career.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British racing driver currently competing in Formula One with the Haas team.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian racing driver Gabi Bortoleto currently competes in Formula One as a member of the Audi team.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Valtteri Bottas, a Finnish racing driver, currently competes in Formula One for Cadillac. The 13-season veteran has secured two runner-up finishes in the drivers' championship during his time with Mercedes in 2019 and 2020, and has claimed 10 Grand Prix victories throughout his career.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Argentine driver Franco Alejandro Colapinto currently races in Formula One with the Alpine team. He represents his country in the sport's top category.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Australian driver Jack Doohan has appeared in seven Formula One races between 2024 and 2025 while maintaining a reserve role at Haas. Outside of his single-seater commitments, he races in the European Le Mans Series' LMP2 category for Nielsen Racing.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. He previously achieved his sole Grand Prix victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix while competing for AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Alexandre Hadjar is a French-Algerian driver who races for Red Bull Racing in Formula One, competing under the French nationality.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Ferrari, holding an unprecedented seven world championship titles that match Michael Schumacher's record. The driver has established numerous records throughout his career, including the most race victories, pole positions, and podium finishes in the sport's history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: Nicolas Hülkenberg is a German driver currently competing in Formula One for Audi. Beyond his single-seater commitments, he achieved significant success in endurance racing, securing victory at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 while driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson, a New Zealand motorsport competitor, currently races in Formula One representing Racing Bulls.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc, a Monégasque driver competing for Ferrari, finished second in the 2022 world championship standings. Throughout his nine seasons in Formula One, he has achieved nine Grand Prix victories.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: K-Mag is a Danish motorsport competitor who raced in Formula One across two separate periods, from 2014-2020 and again in 2022-2024. Currently, he competes in the World Endurance Championship as a BMW factory driver for WRT, while also maintaining a part-time NASCAR commitment with Trackhouse Racing.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris is a British Formula One driver competing for McLaren who claimed the 2025 World Drivers' Championship after securing 13 Grand Prix victories throughout his eight-season career in the sport.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French Formula One driver currently competing for Haas. The driver previously secured a Grand Prix victory at the 2021 Hungarian round while racing for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Sergio Pérez, known as "Checo," brings extensive Formula One experience to Cadillac after competing in the sport for 15 seasons. He finished as championship runner-up in 2023 while driving for Red Bull and has accumulated six Grand Prix victories throughout his career.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Oscar Piastri, an Australian driver competing for McLaren in Formula One, has secured nine Grand Prix victories during his four-year tenure in the sport.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo, an Australian driver known by the nickname "the Honey Badger," competed in Formula One over fourteen years before retiring in 2024, accumulating eight Grand Prix victories during his career in the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: George Russell, a British driver competing for Mercedes, has secured seven Grand Prix victories throughout his eight-year Formula One career.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz competes for Williams in Formula One, where he has accumulated four Grand Prix victories throughout his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver who raced in Formula One during 2023 and 2024 before transitioning to sports car racing. He currently competes in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition, following previous stints in IMSA competition.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian motorsport competitor who currently races for Aston Martin in Formula One.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda, a Japanese racing driver, held a full-time Formula One seat from 2021 to 2025 before transitioning to a reserve role with Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls in 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: The Dutch-Belgian driver competes for Red Bull Racing in Formula One, where he has secured four consecutive world championship titles between 2021 and 2024. Across his 12-season career, Verstappen has accumulated 71 Grand Prix victories.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu, China's sole Formula One competitor to date, raced in the championship from 2022 through 2024 before transitioning to a reserve role with Cadillac. He continues his involvement with the team in a supporting capacity.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based team has competed under the Alpine banner since 2021 as Renault's factory outfit, having previously raced as Renault F1 Team. Following the French manufacturer's withdrawal from the sport at the end of 2025, the squad ended its long association with Groupe Renault and the Renault–Nissan–Mitsubishi Alliance.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin has entered Formula One through multiple iterations as a British manufacturer, with its present squad operating under AMR GP Limited and competing under the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team banner.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of the Italian luxury automaker, represents the sport's longest-continuously competing and most accomplished team, having participated in every Formula One World Championship since the series' inception in 1950. The team's iconic emblem has earned them the colloquial designation "the Prancing Horse" among racing enthusiasts.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: Gene Haas, a NASCAR team owner, founded this American-licensed Formula One outfit in 2014, with racing commencing in 2016. The squad has operated under various naming arrangements and is presently led by team principal Ayao Komatsu, who took over following Guenther Steiner's departure after nearly a decade in charge.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: A Swiss engineering outfit established in 1970, this constructor initially built sports cars before shifting to Formula One machinery as an independent operation. The team competed in the sport from 1993 onwards, winning Le Mans in 1989 and becoming the fourth-longest-serving constructor by race count before ceasing operations in 2025, when Audi acquired the organization to serve as the foundation for its own F1 program.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing is a British Formula One outfit headquartered at its technology facility in Woking that competes under corporate sponsorship. The team operates as part of the broader McLaren Group and is owned by Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: The Mercedes-AMG Petronas Formula One Team, based in Brackley and operating under a German licence, represents the latest iteration of Mercedes-Benz's involvement in Formula One spanning back to 1954 as both constructor and engine supplier. Since 2022, the team has operated under equal ownership among Mercedes-Benz Group, Ineos, and team principal Toto Wolff. Mercedes' racing programmes are traditionally identified by the "Silver Arrows" designation.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that began competing in 2024 as part of Red Bull GmbH's two-team operation alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with a secondary facility near Milton Keynes, the team operates as Red Bull's sister squad within the championship.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor established in 2024, operating as one of two Red Bull-owned squads alongside Red Bull Racing. Headquartered in Faenza with a secondary facility near Milton Keynes, the team represents the Austrian conglomerate's second constructor entry in the sport.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Red Bull Racing, an Austrian-licensed team headquartered in England, has operated as a Formula One competitor since 2005 under the ownership of Red Bull GmbH, which also runs Racing Bulls as its second team entry. Christian Horner led the squad from its inception through 2024, with Laurent Mekies assuming the principal role thereafter.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering Limited, established in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head following the collapse of Williams's prior racing venture, remains a British Formula One team and constructor headquartered in Grove, Oxfordshire. Competing as Atlassian Williams F1 Team in 2026, the operation occupies a substantial 60-acre facility and has maintained its position as a constructor throughout its existence.
